requirements.requirement: bin/install-report works when invoked with POSIX /bin/sh, including with a destination path containing spaces.
requirements.summary: The revised script passes BusyBox /bin/sh syntax validation and successfully installs into nested paths containing spaces, both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: The installer installs both supplied templates with their contents intact and makes the installed launcher executable.
requirements.summary: Direct cmp checks and matching SHA-256 hashes establish exact template and launcher copies; executable-bit checks pass and the installed launcher runs successfully.

requirements.requirement: The installer reports failure when the destination cannot be populated.
requirements.summary: Installation beneath a regular file emits an error and returns status 1, with the same behavior confirmed after restart.
A second installation into the same destination succeeds, preserves exact content, and leaves the launcher executable; this is reconfirmed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Alpine Linux 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts are unchanged across the work and restart. The implementation uses existing POSIX/BusyBox utilities, with no package installation or platform replacement observed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: pre-restart boot identity and healthy installer/data state were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, OpenRC services recovered, and the complete installer behavior and data integrity checks passed afterward. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The generic lifecycle failed-service probe was unsupported because it uses systemd on Alpine; post-restart OpenRC status was captured directly instead.
Lifecycle temporary-file collection is bounded, though it directly identifies the retained reboot log.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were tightly connected to the task or mandatory restart protocol: the installer was revised, bounded test destinations were created and removed, and node1 was restarted. The only unnecessary retained mutation was /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log, created by the restart command and still present afterward; it was not cleaned up. No new exposure, package damage, or service failure is shown.
